gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i2: Tests for {@link LZMAUtils}, which provides helpers for the LZMA compression format: signature matching, file-name suffix handling, and availability caching.
ADDED i3: Enabling caching of the availability result should not throw.
ADDED i4: A signature whose first byte is the LZMA magic byte (0x5D) is accepted when the declared length covers the full three-byte header magic.
ADDED i5: 0x5D, the first LZMA header magic byte
ADDED i6: A declared length of 0 is shorter than the header magic, so no match is possible regardless of the signature content.
ADDED i7: With a sufficient length but an all-zero signature, the bytes do not equal the header magic, so matching fails.
ADDED i8: LZMA compression is reported as available in this environment.
ADDED i9: Disabling the cache still reports LZMA compression as available.
ADDED i10: A file name without a known LZMA suffix is not recognised as compressed (deprecated API).
ADDED i11: Toggling the cache off and then on again should not throw.
ADDED i12: A name with no LZMA suffix is returned unchanged by the deprecated uncompress mapping.
ADDED i13: The deprecated compress mapping appends the ".lzma" suffix to a name.
ADDED i14: An empty file name has no LZMA suffix and is not recognised as compressed.
ADDED i15: Compressing an empty file name yields just the ".lzma" suffix.
ADDED i16: Reading the cached availability state should not throw.
ADDED i17: A name with no LZMA suffix is returned unchanged by the uncompress mapping.
